comparison: Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the crystallographic identification of conserved water networks (C4, C5, C37-C39, C46-C49). OpenEval emphasizes consistency across multiple independent structures (6CN9, 5DRB), while peer reviewers accept the water networks as independently observed without concerns. Complete agreement on this structural finding.

Perfect alignment on PEG400-induced structural changes (C6, C7, C40, C42, C51-C69, C114-C115). Both evaluations accept the crystallographic evidence for space group changes, monomerization, water loss, and conformational changes. Editor explicitly states evidence is 'solid' and OpenEval provides detailed structural validation. Complete agreement.

Both evaluations support the structural characterization of the AL-CL Cluster (C8, C70-C73). OpenEval highlights crystallographic data and sequence conservation analysis, while peer reviewers implicitly accept the identification of six conserved residues lining the CWN1 pocket. Complete agreement on structural characterization.

Strong agreement on activating mutations (C9-C11, C76-C82, C118). Both evaluations accept LC-MS autophosphorylation data and reduced chloride sensitivity for E314Q/A mutants. OpenEval includes C119 (not in peer result) but both support the water-mediated inhibition model. Peer reviewer notes revised manuscript satisfactorily addressed concerns.

Both support the observation of reduced activity mutants (C12, C85-C86, C121-C123), though peer result does not explicitly reference all claims in OpenEval R5 (C83-C84, C88-C89 appear in other peer results). Both acknowledge mechanistic uncertainty appropriately. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED while noting interpretive limitations; peer reviewers accept with acknowledgment of gaps.

Both evaluations address coupling of activity and chloride sensitivity (C13, C124-C127). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to incomplete mechanistic understanding, while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED with appropriate acknowledgment of interpretive gaps. Substantive agreement on data quality but slight difference in evaluation framing—OpenEval emphasizes uncertainty while peer review emphasizes acceptance of demonstrated correlation.

Both support ADP-Glo validation data (C90-C95, C128-C129). OpenEval emphasizes agreement between ADP-Glo and LC-MS methods and notes no single mutant abolishes PEG sensitivity. Peer reviewers note consistency between Figures 6 and 7 measurements and accept osmosensitivity retention. Complete agreement on validation approach.

Both support SLS oligomerization data (C96-C101, C117). OpenEval notes limitations (only two monomeric mutants, most show 50/50 mixtures) while peer reviewers accept varying effects on oligomerization. Both agree SLS data support role of water networks in dimer stabilization. Agreement with OpenEval providing more critical assessment of generalizability.

Both support E314A crystal structure comparison (C15, C45, C103-C107, C120). OpenEval notes limitations (3.4Å resolution, domain-swapped dimer, failure to crystallize WNK1/E388A) while peer reviewers accept structure as supporting the hypothesis. Both rate as SUPPORTED but OpenEval provides more detailed critique of structural limitations.

OpenEval R10 addresses mechanistic speculation about reduced activity (C14, C122-C123) and rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting authors acknowledge this as speculative. Peer R5 partially overlaps (C122-C123) and accepts the acknowledgment of mechanistic uncertainty as appropriate. Agreement that mechanism is unresolved.

Both support the central water-as-allosteric-inhibitor hypothesis (C16, C41, C116, C119/C131). OpenEval emphasizes convergence of multiple evidence lines while noting lack of direct water binding affinity measurement. Peer reviewers accept hypothesis as supported and note considerable interest to the field. Strong agreement on central conclusion.

Perfect agreement on background/context claims from prior literature (C1-C2, C17-C36, C108-C113, C130). Both evaluations accept these as established knowledge appropriately cited. OpenEval notes these are not novel findings; peer reviewer explicitly states prior work is not questioned. Complete agreement.

Both support methodological quality control regarding phosphorylation states (C74 shared, OpenEval includes C43-C44, C75, C160). OpenEval provides detailed documentation while peer reviewers implicitly accept without questioning. Agreement on quality control measures.

OpenEval R14 addresses C61 (reference to prior Akella et al. 2020 work on osmolyte effects), rating as SUPPORTED. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though this prior work is accepted as part of general background in peer R14.

Partial overlap on control mutants K236A and K307A (C83-C84). Both accept these show minimal effects similar to wild-type, helping define functional boundaries of AL-CL Cluster. Peer R9 specifically notes these without concerns; OpenEval R5 includes these among reduced activity mutants discussion.

Partial overlap on S304 phosphorylation data (C88-C89). OpenEval R5 notes parallel effects on S304 and S308 provide internal consistency. Peer R10 accepts S304 data as supporting evidence without questioning. Agreement on data quality.
